comments.content: Static readonly _authNonce generated once at construction defeats CSRF protection. State should be a fresh random value per auth request and single-use. Reusing the same nonce for the service lifetime allows replay attacks and makes the state parameter ineffective.

Prompting user to confirm on state mismatch effectively bypasses CSRF validation. An attacker-controlled callback can present a warning and trick the user into storing a malicious token. If external initiations are needed, use a secure nonce exchange rather than allowing arbitrary state values with user confirmation.

validateAuthState now only compares to a static nonce and no longer resets/clears it. With a static nonce this is a no-op and changes the original one-time validation semantics. If this method is used elsewhere, callers may expect nonce consumption.
